project: Nutrition5k Food Recognition and Calorie Estimation

vit_b16.notes: Transformer model, lower accuracy likely due to limited training data

direct_regression.notes: Best performing method for calorie estimation via evaluate.py
Best method - end-to-end image to calorie

two_stage_gt_category.notes: Uses calorie density lookup table with ground truth categories

category_baseline.notes: Simple baseline using mean calories per food category

end_to_end_multi_task.notes: Model has multiple architectural bugs preventing proper evaluation

key_findings: EfficientNet-B0 achieves 64.05% top-1 accuracy on 154-class food classification
ViT-B/16 achieves 42.16% top-1 accuracy (limited by dataset size)
Direct regression achieves best calorie MAE (94.32 kcal)
Two-stage approach with GT categories: 135.99 kcal MAE
limitations: High MAPE values due to samples with near-zero calorie counts
End-to-end model has multiple architectural bugs
ViT requires more data to reach optimal performance
Segmentation evaluation limited (no ground truth masks in dataset)

evaluation_notes.classifier_evaluation: Fixed backbone detection from state_dict keys (config was incorrect)
evaluation_notes.regression_evaluation: Using pre-computed normalization stats from training data
evaluation_notes.end_to_end_evaluation: Model has architectural bugs - results unreliable

fundamental_issue.training_behavior: Model learns: GT_box → Total_dish_calories (single instance predicts entire dish)
fundamental_issue.inference_behavior: Multiple detected instances each predict 'total dish calories', then aggregated (summed)
fundamental_issue.result: If 3 instances detected, each predicting ~300 kcal (total dish), aggregation gives 900 kcal instead of 300

bugs_fixed_in_retrain: Image normalization consistency between training_forward() and forward()
NaN prevention via gradient clipping (max_grad_norm=1.0) and loss scaling (regression_loss_scale=0.001)
remaining_unfixable_issues: Training uses single GT box per sample but inference detects multiple instances
Model cannot distinguish between 'per-instance calories' vs 'total dish calories'
Aggregation strategy fundamentally incompatible with training objective
end_to_end_architectural_bugs.conclusion: End-to-End model has FUNDAMENTAL ARCHITECTURE MISMATCH that cannot be fixed without redesigning the training approach. The model learns to predict total dish calories from a single box, but inference aggregates multiple such predictions.
end_to_end_architectural_bugs.recommendation: Use Direct Regression model (MAE: 94.32 kcal) for production use. End-to-End approach requires complete redesign.
